name: Octatrack
summary: Effects, machines, MIDI and USB modules built on octabam.

firmware.flash: Copy the .bin to the card root, then PROJECT › SYSTEM › OS UPGRADE.
firmware.recovery: Hold FUNC while powering on, choose MIDI UPGRADE and send the stock .syx over DIN MIDI.

sdk.toolchain: GNU binutils 2.47 (m68k-elf) and the dsp56300 assembler, run in the pinned build container (sdk/build/Dockerfile).

budgets.name: Reserved module memory
budgets.note: The bottom 1,707 pages (6,144 B each) of the audio page arena that the octabam platform reserves for modules.

budgets.name: SRC machine slots

name: Digitakt II
summary: Experimental OS 1.17 support exists in elekloader, with a core and released perform mods. Modwerk integration and qualification are not complete.

firmware.flash: Normal OS updates use Elektron Transfer with the owner's own stock OS file. Modwerk's DTII build path is experimental and downloads remain disabled.
firmware.recovery: Hold FUNC while powering on, choose TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE), then send the owner's stock .syx over MIDI DIN; recovery mode does not use USB.

research.label: digikit
research.note: Emulator for the control processor that boots the real OS and shows its screen, plus analysis tools for the audio processor and the sealed OS file.

research.label: elekloader DTII core and OS 1.17 tests
research.note: Experimental OS 1.17 profile, sealed firmware writer and shared-event core. Its DTII tests verify byte-exact stock rebuilding, seal checks and linked builds. Core builds boot in Digikit; this is not Modwerk hardware qualification.

research.label: toonst's Digitakt II perform mods 1.0
research.note: Released core, perform-direct and perform-levels packages for OS 1.17. The author reports individual hardware results, including an earlier perform-direct version; the combined build is not hardware-tested. Modwerk listings remain to be added.

sdk.toolchain: m68k-elf GCC and binutils, Modwerk's elemod packager, and the vendored elekloader kit 0.5.0; firmware builds start from the owner's exact OS 1.17 .syx.

budgets.name: Shared mod memory
budgets.note: Digitakt II DDR region 0x47F00000–0x47F40000, shared by core and linked mods.

budgets.name: Core image
budgets.note: Core 1.0 build: 480 bytes .run plus 20 bytes .bss; package link check measures each selected module set.

budgets.name: Fast SRAM for code
budgets.note: SRAM tail 0x8000F100–0x80010000; core copies .fast code here on its first UI tick.

budgets.name: Per-event subscriptions
budgets.note: Core 1.0 allocates four hook entries per shared event collection.

name: Digitone II
summary: Shares the Digitakt II platform and its sealed OS file. OS 1.12 rebuilds byte for byte, and a draft core with the Digitakt II's six events runs in the emulator.

firmware.flash: Normal OS updates use Elektron Transfer with the owner's own stock OS file. Modwerk has no Digitone II build path yet and downloads stay disabled.
firmware.recovery: Hold FUNC while powering on, choose TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE), then send the owner's stock .syx over MIDI DIN; recovery mode does not use USB. Not yet tried on a Digitone II.

research.label: Digitone II OS research
research.note: OS 1.12: container, seal, staging, reset memory map, free DDR and SRAM, the seven core sites and the emulator checks. Stock-free: hashes and addresses only.

research.label: digikit
research.note: Emulator for the control processor that boots the real OS and shows its screen, plus analysis tools for the audio processor and the sealed OS file. Supports Digitone II OS 1.11 and 1.12.

research.label: elekloader DTII core
research.note: The Digitakt II core whose events, sources and site patterns the Digitone II draft core reuses with OS 1.12's addresses.

name: Syntakt
summary: OS 1.40, 1.40A and 1.42 documented; 1.40A and 1.42 rebuilt byte-identical; modified builds boot on a unit. Core started: a boot probe links and verifies locally; no SDRAM for mods yet.

firmware.flash: Elektron Transfer over USB: set MIDI IN and OUT to the device, drop the .syx on and confirm on the device.
firmware.recovery: Hold FUNC while powering on to open the STARTUP menu, choose TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE), then send the owner's stock .syx from Transfer's SysEx Transfer / OS Upgrade via device startup menu over MIDI DIN; USB does not work there. Documented by Synthack-OS; this startup-menu path is not yet tested on our unit.

research.label: elektron-firmware-tool
research.note: Writer. Reads Syntakt OS files (device 0x16). Unchanged -r repack is byte-identical (cmp) to stock OS 1.40A and 1.42, checked 2026-10-12.

research.label: Synthack-OS
research.note: MIT mods for OS 1.41 as patch.json with expected-byte hashes, plus modarea/vparams infrastructure. The project states seven mods run on hardware, documents recovery over MIDI DIN, and its issue #4 reports runtime page writes above the BSS on a unit.

research.label: Synthack-OS 1.42 port
research.note: master-comp ported to OS 1.42; the build booted and ran on the author's Syntakt (2026-10-11). No firmware hosted.

research.label: digiemu Syntakt port
research.note: Emulator boots OS 1.40A to the live UI with the second ColdFire rendering its digital machines; analog tracks and the FPGA are not modelled. Open PR.

research.label: Modwerk Syntakt OS research
research.note: Static analysis of the owner's 1.40 and 1.42 files: boot chain, memory ownership with verdicts, hook sites with guards, cross-release diff, the boot-probe core. Nothing run on a unit.

name: Tonverk
summary: Multitimbral sampler. OS 1.4.1 update container documented: SWUpdate .swu, encrypted payloads, signed boot chain, strong stock recovery. No mod route yet.

research.label: Elektron Tonverk release notes
research.note: OS 1.0.0-1.4.1 history; .swu updates from the SD card root through USB disk mode and SETTINGS > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE; downgrading unsupported.

research.label: Elektron Tonverk downloads
research.note: The OS 1.4.1 zip and manuals this research inspected; identities are recorded in docs/TONVERK_OS_RESEARCH.md.

research.label: SWUpdate
research.note: The .swu container convention the Tonverk update follows: cpio archive, sw-description manifest, preinst/postinst hooks, signatures and encrypted artifacts.

research.label: U-Boot FIT documentation
research.note: The FIT image and signed boot-script format the readable Tonverk bootscript uses (mkimage 2025.04, sha256,rsa3072).

name: Analog Rytm
summary: OS 1.74 rebuilt byte-identical; modified OSes boot on hardware; stock recovers over MIDI DIN; core-ar2 0.3 with mod storage runs on units. Filter Hz is the first library module.

firmware.flash: Elektron Transfer over USB: set MIDI IN and OUT to the device, drop the .syx on and press YES on the device. It restarts by itself.
firmware.recovery: Recovery mode is MIDI DIN ONLY — it does NOT work over USB: the startup menu never enumerates USB, so once a non-stock OS is on the unit a MIDI-DIN sender is REQUIRED (a USB-MIDI interface, or a hand-wired FT232RL serial adapter at 31250 baud: +5V/220 ohm to DIN 4, TXD/220 ohm to DIN 5, GND to DIN 2, raw .syx). Hold FUNC at power-on, TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE), send the owner's stock .syx.

research.label: rytm-fw-re
research.note: Static analysis of OS 1.74: format, boot contract, startup-menu recovery, display pipeline, plus a from-source replacement OS. Hardware-verified: flashed over USB, booted (display + memory probe), recovered to stock 1.74 over MIDI DIN via a hand-wired FT232RL adapter. No firmware hosted.

research.label: elektron-firmware-tool
research.note: Writer. Verified on OS 1.74: unchanged repack is byte-identical to the stock file (sysex re-encode and aPLib recompression included); section replacement round-trips exactly on re-extract.

research.label: rytm-mods-src
research.note: MrScruff's OS 1.73 mod build, published with permission. make verify rebuilds the stock .syx byte for byte and asserts that only MAIN OS changes; eight of its twelve mods are marked hardware-verified by their author. No firmware hosted.

research.label: rytm-mods-boot-report
research.note: Stock OS 1.73 .syx rebuilt byte-identical by elektron-firmware-tool (matching SHA-256). A build of rytm-mods-src cf5ac006 then booted on an MKII with 0008-filter-hz working, and the stock .syx restored it. Also shows 1.74 to 1.73 over USB and DIN. Hashes and photos only.

research.label: elekloader core-ar2
research.note: Device profile and core for OS 1.73: elekloader's Digitakt mk1 core built with the Rytm's addresses. Byte-exact writer, flash limit and DDR area evidenced; boot, tick, draw, key, encoder, SETTINGS and render events run on a unit. No firmware hosted.

research.label: rytm-mods-boot-report: core
research.note: Hardware report for the core: builds HM01 (core + hello-marker) and HC01 (core + hooks-check) on OS 1.73, every event observed, plus the DDR-area canary and render-site probes from rytm-mods-src's elemod branch. Hashes and photos only.

research.label: rytm-emu
research.note: Emulator for the Analog Rytm and Analog Four, MKI and MKII (a fork of rouletrro, MIT). Boots stock Rytm MKII OS 1.73 and builds patched from it headless or in a window, with the analog voices stubbed. No firmware hosted.

research.label: rytm2_mods
research.note: All eleven of rytm-mods-src's OS 1.73 mods ported to elemod for core-ar2, MrScruff's code unchanged and checked label by label against his build; each confirmed on a unit. Release v1.0. No firmware hosted.

sdk.toolchain: m68k-linux-gnu (or m68k-elf) GCC and binutils for ColdFire, and elekloader's builder: core-ar2 0.3 from the owner's exact OS 1.74 .syx.

budgets.name: Shared mod memory
budgets.note: DDR 0x47BE0000–0x47C00000, shared by the core and every mod; a boot-time fill was read back intact on a unit (DDR-area canary, elekloader core-ar2 evidence).

budgets.name: Core image
budgets.note: Core 0.3 build (core-ar2-v0.3 pre-release): 7,540 bytes .run plus 36 bytes .bss in the shared area, and an 88-byte .boot copier; the link check measures each selected module set.

name: Analog Four
summary: OS 1.56 rebuilt byte-identical; modified OSes boot on hardware; stock recovers over MIDI DIN; core-a4 0.2 (the Rytm's core, with mod storage and parameter pages) runs on a unit.

firmware.flash: Elektron Transfer over USB: set MIDI IN and OUT to the device, drop the .syx on and press YES on the device. It restarts by itself.
firmware.recovery: Recovery mode is MIDI DIN only, as on the Analog Rytm MKII: hold FUNC at power-on for the STARTUP menu, press TRIG 4 (OS UPGRADE) and send the owner's stock .syx over MIDI DIN (a USB-MIDI interface or a serial adapter at 31250 baud), not USB.

research.label: elektron-firmware-tool
research.note: Container and SysEx transport. OS 1.56 unpacks to five sections (meta, bootstrap, FPGA, packed main OS, ARM) with every checksum valid, and an unchanged repack is byte-identical to the stock file.

research.label: elekloader analog-four-mk2
research.note: Device profile for OS 1.56: the Analog Rytm MKII's platform, OS entry and bootstrap loader matched instruction for instruction; the writer rebuilds the stock file byte for byte; flash limit, no protected range and the mods' DDR area evidenced; DIN recovery checked on a unit. No firmware hosted.

research.label: elekloader core-a4
research.note: core-ar2 on OS 1.56 (irpina/elekloader#180). On a unit: HC56 ran every event; SC56 kept mod storage through saves, loads and power cycles; CA56 left the mods' area intact; PA56 (core 0.2) passed the parameter page checks; stock 1.56 restored it. No firmware hosted.

research.label: analog-emu
research.note: rytm-emu fork that boots stock Analog Four MKII OS 1.56 to its main UI, headless or in a window, with the analog voices stubbed; used for the core's emulator checks before each hardware run. No firmware hosted.

sdk.toolchain: m68k-linux-gnu (or m68k-elf) GCC and binutils for ColdFire, and elekloader's builder: core-a4 0.2 from the owner's exact OS 1.56 .syx.

budgets.name: Shared mod memory
budgets.note: DDR 0x47BE0000–0x47C00000, shared by the core and every mod; a fill of the area and its neighbouring gaps read back intact on a unit through normal use and a power cycle (elekloader ddr-canary-a4).

budgets.name: Core image
budgets.note: Core 0.2 build (elekloader f02be99): 8,764 bytes .run plus 192 bytes .bss in the shared area, and an 88-byte .boot copier; the link check measures each selected module set.

name: Analog Keys
summary: OS 1.56 is an ELE2 image whose MAIN OS section rebuilds byte-identically. A modified OS boots: ours in rytm-emu, and a third party's on A4/Keys MK1 hardware, 2026-10-17.

firmware.flash: Elektron Transfer over USB: set MIDI IN and OUT to the device, drop the .syx and press YES on the unit. Or from the STARTUP menu: hold FUNC at power-on, choose OS UPGRADE with TRIG 4, and send the .syx from Transfer's LEGACY OS UPGRADE mode over MIDI DIN.
firmware.recovery: Hold FUNC at power-on to reach the STARTUP menu and send the owner's stock .syx over MIDI DIN; the startup menu does not enumerate USB, so the DIN path is required. Do not power the unit off until it has finished the bootstrap upgrade that follows the first restart after some upgrades. Elektron states the Analog Keys cannot be downgraded below OS 1.1.

research.label: elektron-firmware-tool
research.note: MIT. Reads, verifies, extracts and rewrites this image's ELE2 container and Adler-32 section checksum unchanged; a verbatim section repack is byte-identical to stock OS 1.56. No firmware hosted.

research.label: AE-analog-four-mods
research.note: Mods for the Analog Four / Keys MK1 on OS 1.56: verified symbol map, free-space registry, byte-checked build, and a modded OS booted on MK1 hardware on 2026-10-17. Supplies the boot step's evidence. No firmware hosted.

research.label: rytm-emu
research.note: MIT. Boots stock OS 1.56 for the Analog Four MKI and the Analog Keys to its main screen, headless or in a window. Our local branch adds DTEMU_PROFILE to run a modified image by name; nothing pushed.

firmware.recovery: Remove the effect in Effect Manager. If a bad effect freezes the pedal at boot, run All Initialize (hold the leftmost knob while powering on), then remove the effect.
